header.stance: 股市反彈、短債殖利率回升，長天期美債守穩

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 股市與油價反彈，短天期美債小幅走弱

週一股市反彈、油價上漲，區域製造業調查的招聘與售價也轉強，短天期美債吐回部分週五漲幅。2年期殖利率上升3個基點至4.10%，5年期上升2個基點至4.14%；10年期維持4.38%，30年期下降1個基點至4.86%，曲線趨平。

10年期名目殖利率不變，內部組成卻再次調整。實質殖利率下降2個基點至2.16%，損益兩平通膨率上升2個基點至2.22%，兩者互相抵銷。前一個月能源成本下降仍有利債券，但當日油價回升、西班牙通膨高於預期，提醒市場價格壓力尚未消失。達拉斯Fed調查同樣呈現產出與訂單轉慢，就業與成品售價卻轉強的落差。

最高法院以狹義程序理由，允許Fed理事Lisa Cook在挑戰免職期間留任，解除了眼前職位被撤換的威脅。7月2日交割前，大額國庫券供給仍順利標售，公司債ETF也隨股市上漲。個別信用事件差異更大：私募信貸基金推介新債，Charter因整併預期走強，TPx進入Chapter 11。股票融資成本上升，則使市場更關注季底時交易商還能提供多少債券與附買回融通。

## 工廠產出放緩，招聘與價格卻更強

達拉斯Fed 6月生產指數下降5點至4.1，新訂單由6.4降至2.3，一般企業活動維持零。就業指數卻由0.2跳升至13.9，工時升至5.9；成品價格增加10點至28.6，原料價格仍高達42.4。Fed看到的是生產較慢，企業仍積極用工並提高售價。

相較前一週漲勢，當天美債調整幅度不大。2、5、10及30年期殖利率仍比一週前低14、15、13及9個基點。週一2年與10年期利差收窄3個基點至28，2年與30年期收窄4個基點至76。實質殖利率各天期下降：5及7年期各跌1個基點，至1.90%及2.02%；20與30年期也各跌1個基點，至2.49%及2.68%。短天期名目券的弱勢沒有擴及實質殖利率。

Cook案涉及另一項政策制度問題。最高法院以5比4裁定，她可以留任，同時挑戰川普基於未經證實房貸指控所提出的免職。多數意見指出，總統未事先通知，也未給她陳述機會。法院並未判定指控若屬實，是否足以構成免職理由，後續仍可能繼續訴訟。

### 季底供給與交易商資產負債表

財政部標售$920億91天期國庫券，最高得標利率3.740%，投標倍數2.32，最高利率分配比例85.81%。間接投標人取得$362.93億，直接投標人$62.85億，交易商$459.97億。$790億182天期則在3.840%得標，投標倍數2.58，最高利率分配比例96.12%；間接、直接及交易商分別承接$431.80億、$54.99億及$278.63億。6個月期投標較強、留給交易商較少，兩券都在7月2日交割。

次級國庫券的壓力主要在較長一點的天期。4及6週期息票等值殖利率各上升1個基點，至3.69%及3.68%，8週期維持3.73%；13週期上升8個基點至3.83%，17、26及52週期分別上升3、4及3個基點，至3.88%、3.97%及3.96%。供給與交割日期接近，正好遇上這段上升，Fed利率路徑也仍偏緊。

股票融資正在競爭交易商的資產負債表。S&P 500總報酬期貨7月合約的融資報價，6月26日達到200個基點，5月平均為62個基點。BofA策略師Eleanor Xiao與Mark Cabana警告，若壓力持續，交易商可能把容量由固定收益移向股票。資金流入貨幣市場基金，有助緩和附買回壓力，但較後季度的期貨仍反映比5月更高的融資成本。

大型股票發行解釋了部分需求。截至6月26日，美國IPO與增資達創紀錄的$2,510億，不含空白支票公司與投資工具，超過2021年上半年高點；SpaceX $862億上市與Alphabet $850億增資占了很大部分，AI支出也預期支持可轉債發行。大型交易完成後，可能釋出部分現金，高估值與槓桿基金成長仍持續占用容量。

## 新融資重返市場，個別債券由事件帶動

Morgan Stanley Direct Lending Fund推介$3.5億5年期債券，初始價格討論約為美債加245個基點，是逾一年來首次發債。所得將用於再融資，可能包含Truist Financial及BNP Paribas的循環額度。私募信貸貸款品質與軟體曝險受到更多檢視後，這筆交易測試買方對業務開發公司（BDC）的需求。T. Rowe Price私募信貸基金前一週$4億首筆發行，訂單高峰超過3倍；Morgan Stanley這筆仍待最終定價。

Charter票息7%、2033年到期的無擔保券，最多上漲4.125美分、逼近面額，創發行以來最大漲幅。5年期CDS最多收窄66個基點至290，為歷來最大盤中改善。市場押注Comcast分拆後可能出現整併，並期待其資產負債表有助緩解Charter的競爭與槓桿壓力。交易尚未發生，漲勢仍取決於不確定的企業行動。

TPx Communications在多次重整及漏付第一順位利息後，帶著$11億有息債務進入Chapter 11。方案包括$2,000萬破產期間融資、$5,350萬舊債轉入，以及出售程序。若未出售，公司目標以約$1.29億負債出場，減債約$10億。EBITDA為正，仍不足以支撐原本資本結構。

Raizen公布2026年前3個月消耗R$34億現金。債權人已批准這家糖與燃料生產商約R$650億庭外重整，方案將45%債務轉為約80%股權，並包含Shell R$35億注資。更大的資產減損及持續現金流出，讓回收前景更複雜。多數重整債務分配至燃料配送業務，因此預計至2027年底的分拆，將影響營運表現與債權價值。

### 銀行資本利差收斂，中國信評面臨檢視

不同次順位銀行發行人的定價差距大幅縮小。大型歐洲AT1重設利差的標準差，2026年降至略高於52個基點，一年前逾110；最寬新券利差由接近1,000降至520個基點，最窄則仍約250。美國特別股利差分散程度也減半以上至約46個基點。對獲利與曝險不同的銀行，投資人要求的補償愈來愈接近。

歐元AT1重設利差集中在300多個基點的較低端，Erste Group交易為307.5個基點，整體到贖回日殖利率平均5.85%。美元避險後全年報酬逾3%，超過類似全球投資級指數的兩倍。強勁表現維持買盤，但未如預期贖回、獲利能力與能源密集借款人曝險等差異，在收窄的利差範圍內較難看出。

中國面對的則是評級過度集中。監理機關加強檢視、資產管理業者重新評估持債後，前一週至少20家公司撤除本地評級，常以自身安排為由。第1季末約6,000家發行人中，逾四分之一是AAA、另32%為AA+；美國流通公司債中，AAA不到1%。在本地公司債殖利率已降至歷史低點的背景下，撤評反而可能減少可供投資人判斷信用差異的資訊。

公司債ETF隨股市上漲，LQD漲0.18%，HYG漲0.23%，JNK漲0.19%。整體買氣改善，個別債券的表現仍取決於新債條件、整併前景與重整回收率。

## 西班牙通膨高於預期，歐洲招聘計畫轉弱

西班牙6月整體通膨維持3.6%，高於調查中位數3.4%。電力及天然氣成本，抵銷了汽油降價帶來的緩解；本國基礎物價指標則降至2.9%。西班牙央行預估2026年成長2.3%、2027年1.7%。油價下降已有助益，較廣泛的價格與活動資料，仍未顯示通膨會快速退去。

歐盟執委會歐元區經濟信心指數上升1.3點至95.0，就業預期卻下降2.2點至92.2，兩者都低於長期標準100。ECB委員Martins Kazaks表示，沒有必要快速連續升息多次。決策者可以再觀察，較弱招聘意願是否逐漸減輕仍偏高的價格壓力。

外資5月淨賣出£55億英債，結束從8月開始的買進紀錄，政治不穩定壓過較高殖利率的吸引力。本地投資人淨買入£191億。約三分之一英債由外國人持有，即使本地買盤超過外流，供給承接仍更加依賴國內投資人。

日圓在紐約貶至161.96兌$1，創1986年以來最低，即使日本央行6月稍早已升息至1%。當局4月28日至5月27日才動用創紀錄的¥11.73兆支撐匯率。新一輪貶值，使輸入性通膨與可能干預，再度成為升息討論旁的重要因素。

日本5月零售月增1.9%，前月也獲上修；年增5.3%，高於預估3%。藥妝店年增逾7%，便利商店較慢。薪資成長超過通膨、政府補貼共同支撐支出，這些支持消退後，需求能維持多久仍是央行需要觀察的事。

一位前日本央行主管在週一訪問中主張，12月以前應再升息，因為金融情勢仍過度寬鬆。他把4年平均約3%的基礎通膨，與受補貼壓低的5月核心CPI 1.4%對照，也批評2027會計年度起每月仍購債約¥2兆的安排。這是外部人士觀點，並非日本央行目前指引。

紐約收盤後另有兩項資料。5月失業率維持2.5%，就業人數比一年前增加52萬；工業生產月增0.5%、年減1.7%，製造商預估6月增加3.7%、7月持平。資料更新的是下一個亞洲時段，呈現勞動穩定、工廠復甦不均的情況。

澳洲則公布為未來衰退、傳統降息空間耗盡時準備的框架。現金利率仍是主要工具，另外可使用定期融資、購債、市場操作、前瞻指引、殖利率目標與負利率。助理總裁Christopher Kent認為，除了修復嚴重市場失靈，額外效益可能有限；成本、金融穩定、溝通及退場都須一開始納入設計。疫情期間融資、指引與殖利率目標造成的限制，是這套預備框架的背景，並非當前寬鬆決策。

## 原油進口國受惠，印度吸引更強外資買盤

肯亞與剛果民主共和國，是油價下跌後表現領先的非洲債市。6月報酬分別為2%及1.95%，約為新興市場平均兩倍，扭轉部分戰時偏好奈及利亞等出口國的交易。剛果銅礦、鈷礦及消費燃料補貼，尤其受能源成本影響。週一油價反彈，仍未消除更大的月跌幅。

印度可納入指數的政府債，6月外資持有增加3,970億盧比、約$42億，在稅制調整及擴大合格券後，月買超有望創紀錄。包括Danny Suwanapruti在內的高盛分析師偏好30年期，因更多長債進入完全開放管道（FAR），短端則已隨油價下跌與升息預期減少而大幅上漲。

高盛報告認為，最終納入彭博全球綜合債券指數的可能性增加，年中可能宣布。按合格流通債規模估算，權重約0.7%，分階段納入期間可能吸引約$150億被動資金。這是尚待納入的估計，須與6月已記錄的外資買進區別。

巴西為正常還款的非正式就業者推出補貼再融資，月利率1.99%，可展延6個月，貸款上限R$1.5萬。Banco do Brasil與Caixa Economica Federal將提供貸款，目標受惠者20萬至50萬人。計畫部長Bruno Moretti估計利息補貼R$40億，並表示不會改變今年財政目標。另項安排允許以FGTS資遣基金餘額，擔保薪資扣款貸款最多50%。

方案推出時，通膨4.8%高於3%目標，央行才降息25個基點至14.25%。官員曾警告財政刺激可能妨礙通膨下降；財政部長Dario Durigan反駁這種說法，認為方案只是替既有、正常履約的債務降低利率。除了已編列補貼，真正影響政策的是家庭還款負擔減輕後，會增加多少需求。

中國直接處理半年底資金需求。人民銀行透過隔夜逆回購提供人民幣3,000億，7天期操作另提供1,575億。隔夜利率據報1.25%，低於預估中位數1.35%，7天期維持1.4%。較大隔夜操作支撐半年底貨幣市場。美元走低之際，EMB上漲0.29%，各地支持來源則相當不同。

## 股市回升、波動降低，油價小幅走高

S&P 500上漲1.18%，Nasdaq 100上漲2.25%，半導體指數上漲3.83%，收復前一週部分科技跌幅。VIX下降4.13%至17.65。風險偏好改善，同時2及5年期殖利率上升，較長天期美債仍守住價格。

美伊雙方停止攻擊、船隻持續通過荷莫茲海峽，市場等待新一輪談判，WTI上漲2.20%至$70.75，布蘭特上漲1.61%至$73.15。兩者一個月仍下跌19.01%及20.53%。當日反彈伴隨通膨補償上升，未扭轉此前能源價格緩解。

DXY下降0.25%至101.11，黃金下跌1.38%至$4,022.30。波動率與黃金降低、股市及公司債與新興市場債券上漲，顯示眼前保護需求減少。美債曲線的小幅趨平，也發生在這樣的風險偏好回升之中。

## 勞動、歐洲通膨與季底資金考驗

6月30日美東10:00公布JOLTS與Conference Board消費者信心，10:30接續達拉斯Fed零售調查。7月1日有ADP、紐約Fed勞動緊俏指標、營建支出及ISM製造業，2日8:30公布非農與初領失業救濟金。招聘、職缺與售價，將顯示達拉斯強勁就業是否擴及其他地區。

德國失業與CPI初值6月30日公布，歐元區HICP初值7月1日公布，辛特拉論壇也持續。美伊預定在杜哈恢復談判，荷莫茲船運仍是能源展望關鍵。7月1日日本央行短觀，另為日圓與政策討論加入企業投資及價格預期。

財政部6月30日標售$800億6週期國庫券，7月1日進行例行17週期標售，2日美東11:30標售4及8週期。週一91及182天期也在7月2日交割，當天非農早於標售，固定收益市場預定14:00收盤。國庫券殖利率、交易商承接及擔保融資，將顯示貨幣市場基金流入能否持續抵銷股票融資競爭，順利度過集中的資金移轉。

overall_summary.headline: 股市反彈、短債走弱，製造業招聘與售價轉強
overall_summary.session_narrative:
週一股市與油價反彈，短天期美債吐回部分週五漲幅。2年期殖利率上升3個基點至4.10%，10年期維持4.38%：通膨補償增加2個基點，正好抵銷實質殖利率下降。達拉斯製造業產出與訂單放緩，招聘及成品售價卻更強。

信用市場仍可取得融資，個別券表現則分歧。Morgan Stanley Direct Lending Fund推介5年期新債，Charter因整併預期上漲，TPx卻帶著$11億債務進入破產程序。Raizen的現金消耗增加重整的不確定性，銀行資本債的利差差距則持續收斂，較難反映不同發行人的條件。

西班牙通膨高於預期，歐洲招聘計畫卻轉弱。印度6月已吸引$42億外資買進政府債；高盛另估計的$150億被動資金，仍以未來納入指數為前提。接下來美國就業、歐洲通膨與季底資金需求，將集中在7月2日提早收盤前。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Short Treasuries Slip as Stocks and Oil Rebound

Short-dated Treasuries gave back some of Friday's gains Monday as equities rebounded, oil rose and a regional factory survey showed firmer hiring and selling prices. The two-year yield increased 3 basis points to 4.10% and the five-year added 2 to 4.14%. The 10-year held at 4.38%, while the 30-year fell 1 basis point to 4.86%, flattening the curve.

The unchanged 10-year concealed another shift between its components: real yields declined 2 basis points to 2.16%, offset by a 2-basis-point rise in breakeven inflation to 2.22%. Cheaper energy over the preceding month still supported bonds, but Monday's oil bounce and unexpectedly high Spanish inflation cautioned against assuming that price pressure was disappearing. The Dallas Fed survey likewise paired slower output and orders with stronger employment and finished-goods prices.

The Supreme Court allowed Fed Governor Lisa Cook to remain in office while contesting her removal, resolving the immediate threat to her position on narrow procedural grounds. Meanwhile, large bill auctions cleared ahead of July 2 settlement, and corporate funds rose with stocks. Individual credit events were more varied: a private-credit fund marketed new bonds, Charter rallied on merger speculation, and TPx entered Chapter 11. Rising equity-financing costs added a separate concern about how much dealer capacity would remain available for bonds and repo around quarter-end.

## Prices and Hiring Firm Even as Factory Output Slows

The Dallas Fed production index fell 5 points to 4.1 in June and new orders eased to 2.3 from 6.4. General business activity was unchanged at zero. Employment, however, jumped to 13.9 from 0.2 and hours worked rose to 5.9. Finished-goods prices increased 10 points to 28.6, with raw-material prices still elevated at 42.4. The survey gave the Fed evidence of weaker production alongside active hiring and renewed pricing power.

Treasury moves were small against the preceding rally. Two-, five-, 10- and 30-year yields remained 14, 15, 13 and 9 basis points below a week earlier. On Monday, 2s10s narrowed 3 basis points to 28 and 2s30s narrowed 4 to 76. Real yields declined across the curve: five- and seven-year yields each fell 1 basis point to 1.90% and 2.02%, while 20- and 30-year yields each eased 1 to 2.49% and 2.68%. The weakness in short nominal notes did not extend to real yields.

The Cook ruling addressed a different policy issue. By 5-4, the Supreme Court said she could stay while challenging President Donald Trump's attempt to remove her over unproven mortgage allegations. The majority faulted the lack of notice and an opportunity to be heard. It did not decide whether the allegations, if true, would justify dismissal, and further litigation remained possible.

### Quarter-End Supply and Dealer Capacity

Treasury sold $92 billion of 91-day bills at 3.740%, with 2.32 bid-to-cover and 85.81% allotted at the high rate. Indirect bidders took $36.293 billion, direct bidders $6.285 billion and dealers $45.997 billion. The $79 billion 182-day sale stopped at 3.840%, with 2.58 cover and 96.12% allotted at the high. Its indirect, direct and dealer awards were $43.180 billion, $5.499 billion and $27.863 billion. The six-month sale drew stronger coverage and left less with dealers; both issues settle July 2.

Secondary bill yields showed more pressure beyond the very shortest maturities. Four- and six-week coupon-equivalent yields each rose 1 basis point to 3.69% and 3.68%, with eight weeks unchanged at 3.73%. The 13-week rose 8 basis points to 3.83%; 17-, 26- and 52-week yields increased 3, 4 and 3 basis points to 3.88%, 3.97% and 3.96%. Supply and the approaching settlement date coincided with that rise, while the Fed path remained restrictive.

Equity financing was competing for dealer balance sheet. The July S&P 500 total-return futures financing quote touched 200 basis points on June 26, versus a 62-basis-point May average. Bank of America strategists Eleanor Xiao and Mark Cabana warned that continued pressure could draw dealer capacity from fixed income toward equities. Money flowing into money-market funds had helped contain repo pressure, but later quarterly futures still priced more expensive financing than in May.

The scale of share sales explained part of the demand. US IPOs and follow-ons reached a record $251 billion through June 26, excluding blank-check companies and investment vehicles, exceeding the previous first-half high in 2021. SpaceX's $86.2 billion listing and Alphabet's $85 billion raise accounted for much of it, while AI spending was expected to keep convertible issuance active. Completion of large offerings could release some cash, though high valuations and leveraged-fund growth continued to use capacity.

## New Funding Returns, While Event Risk Drives Individual Bonds

Morgan Stanley Direct Lending Fund marketed a proposed $350 million five-year note at initial talk of about 245 basis points over Treasuries, its first bond offering in just over a year. Proceeds would refinance borrowings that could include revolvers with Truist Financial and BNP Paribas. The deal tested demand for a business development company after greater scrutiny of private-credit loans and software exposure. A T. Rowe Price private-credit fund's $400 million debut the previous week had drawn peak orders above three times the amount sold; the Morgan Stanley transaction still awaited final pricing.

Charter's 7% unsecured bond due in 2033 rose as much as 4.125 cents toward par, its biggest gain since issuance. Five-year CDS tightened by as much as 66 basis points to 290, a record intraday improvement. Traders were betting on a possible combination tied to a Comcast breakup and the prospect that Comcast's balance sheet could help Charter's competitive and leverage problems. No transaction had occurred, leaving the rally dependent on an uncertain corporate outcome.

TPx Communications entered Chapter 11 with $1.1 billion of funded debt after repeated restructurings and a missed first-lien interest payment. Its plan included a $20 million debtor-in-possession loan, a $53.5 million roll-up and a sale process. Without a sale, it aimed to emerge with about $129 million of debt, roughly $1 billion less. Positive EBITDA had not been enough to sustain the old capital structure.

Raizen reported 3.4 billion reais of cash burn in the first three months of 2026. Creditors approved the sugar and fuels producer's out-of-court plan covering about 65 billion reais, converting 45% of debt into roughly 80% of equity and including 3.5 billion reais from Shell. A larger impairment charge and continued cash use complicated recovery. Most restructured debt was allocated to fuel distribution, making the planned separation through end-2027 important to both operating performance and creditor value.

### Bank Capital Prices Converge as Chinese Ratings Face Scrutiny

Pricing differences among junior bank issues have narrowed sharply. The standard deviation of reset spreads on large European AT1 sales fell to just over 52 basis points in 2026 from more than 110 a year earlier. The widest new reset spread declined to 520 from nearly 1,000, while the tightest remained around 250. US preferred-share dispersion more than halved to about 46 basis points. Investors were demanding increasingly similar compensation from banks with different earnings and exposures.

Euro AT1 reset spreads clustered in the low 300s, including Erste Group's 307.5-basis-point deal, while average yield to call was 5.85%. Dollar-hedged returns exceeded 3% for the year, more than twice a comparable global investment-grade index. The strong performance helped sustain demand, with call risk, earnings strength and exposure to energy-intensive borrowers less visible in the compressed spread range.

China was confronting compressed ratings rather than compressed bank-capital spreads. At least 20 companies dropped domestic ratings in the preceding week, often citing their own arrangements, as regulators increased scrutiny and asset managers reviewed holdings. More than a quarter of roughly 6,000 issuers were AAA and another 32% AA+ at the first-quarter end; fewer than 1% of outstanding US corporate bonds carried AAA. Withdrawals may complicate investors' ability to distinguish improving disclosure from concealed deterioration, especially after a rally drove domestic corporate yields to record lows.

Broad funds advanced: LQD gained 0.18%, HYG 0.23% and JNK 0.19%. The common positive direction accompanied the equity recovery, while the new deals, event-driven gains and restructurings showed why individual terms still mattered.

## Spain's Inflation Surprise Meets Weaker European Hiring Plans

Spanish headline inflation held at 3.6% in June against a 3.4% median estimate. Electricity and natural-gas costs outweighed restraint from gasoline, while a national underlying measure eased to 2.9%. Spain's central bank projected growth of 2.3% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027. Lower oil had helped, but the country's broader price and activity figures gave little reason to expect a quick retreat in inflation.

The European Commission's euro-area Economic Sentiment Indicator rose 1.3 points to 95.0, while Employment Expectations fell 2.2 to 92.2; both stayed below their long-run norm of 100. ECB Governing Council member Martins Kazaks said several increases in quick succession were unnecessary. The mix left policymakers with time to assess softer hiring intentions against still-firm prices.

Foreign investors sold a net £5.5 billion of gilts in May, ending a buying streak dating to August, as UK political instability outweighed higher yields. Domestic investors bought a net £19.1 billion. With foreigners holding roughly one-third of the market, the shift placed more of the supply burden on local buyers even though their purchases more than offset the outflow.

Japan's yen reached 161.96 per dollar in New York, its weakest since 1986, despite the BOJ's rise to 1% earlier in June. Authorities had already spent a record ¥11.73 trillion supporting the currency from April 28 to May 27. The renewed weakness kept imported inflation and possible intervention prominent alongside the debate over further rate increases.

May retail sales rose 1.9% from April, after an upward revision to the preceding month, and 5.3% over a year against a 3% forecast. Drugstore sales gained more than 7%, while convenience stores grew more slowly. Wages rising faster than inflation and government subsidies supported spending; the durability of demand after that support fades remains relevant to the BOJ.

A former BOJ executive argued in a Monday interview for another increase before December, citing financial conditions that remained too easy. He contrasted an underlying inflation measure averaging about 3% over four years with May's subsidy-restrained 1.4% core CPI and criticized keeping monthly bond purchases around ¥2 trillion from fiscal 2027. His was an outside view, rather than current BOJ guidance.

Two later releases updated the next Asian session. May unemployment held at 2.5%, with employment up 520,000 over a year. Industrial production rose 0.5% monthly but fell 1.7% annually; manufacturers forecast a 3.7% June increase and no July change. These figures arrived after the New York close and combined stable labor conditions with an uneven factory recovery.

Australia published a framework for a future downturn in which conventional cuts might be exhausted. The cash rate remains the main tool, with term funding, bond purchases, market operations, forward guidance, yield targets and negative rates available as additions. Assistant Governor Christopher Kent said benefits beyond repairing severe dysfunction were likely to be marginal. Costs, financial stability, communication and exit needed consideration from the start, reflecting the constraints created by pandemic-era funding, guidance and yield targets. The framework was a contingency plan, not a current easing decision.

## Oil Importers Gain; India Attracts a Stronger Foreign Bid

Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo were among the leading African debt markets as lower oil benefited importers. Their June returns were 2% and 1.95%, roughly twice the EM average, reversing part of the wartime preference for exporters such as Nigeria. Fuel costs matter particularly to Congo's copper and cobalt mines and its consumer subsidies. Monday's oil bounce left the much larger monthly decline intact.

Foreign holdings of India's index-eligible government debt rose 397 billion rupees, or $4.2 billion, during June, putting the month on course for record purchases after tax changes and expanded eligibility. Goldman Sachs analysts including Danny Suwanapruti favored 30-year bonds as more long debt entered the fully accessible route and the front end had already rallied with lower oil and fewer hike expectations.

Their note viewed eventual inclusion in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index as increasingly likely, with a midyear announcement possible. Based on outstanding eligible bonds, Goldman estimated a weight near 0.7% and about $15 billion of passive inflows during the phase-in. That is an estimate tied to prospective inclusion, distinct from June's already recorded foreign purchases.

Brazil announced subsidized refinancing for informal workers current on payments, at 1.99% per month, with six-month extensions and loans up to 15,000 reais eligible. Banco do Brasil and Caixa Economica Federal would offer the credit, targeting 200,000-500,000 beneficiaries. Planning Minister Bruno Moretti put the interest subsidy at 4 billion reais and said it would not alter the year's fiscal target. A separate provision would allow FGTS severance balances to guarantee up to 50% of payroll-deducted loans.

The program arrived with inflation at 4.8%, above the 3% target, after the central bank's quarter-point cut to 14.25%. Officials had warned that fiscal stimulus could complicate disinflation. Finance Minister Dario Durigan rejected that characterization, saying the program refinanced existing, performing debt at lower rates. The policy question is how much the reduction in household debt service adds to demand, alongside the budgeted subsidy.

China acted directly on seasonal funding. The PBOC supplied 300 billion yuan through overnight reverse repos and 157.5 billion through seven-day operations. The overnight rate was reported at 1.25%, below the 1.35% median forecast, while seven days remained 1.4%. The larger overnight operation supported money markets at the half-year turn. EMB gained 0.29% as the dollar eased, alongside these differing local sources of support.

## Stocks Recover and Volatility Falls as Oil Edges Higher

The S&P 500 rose 1.18%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 2.25% and semiconductors advanced 3.83%, recovering part of the previous week's technology losses. VIX declined 4.13% to 17.65. The stronger risk appetite coincided with higher two- and five-year yields, while longer Treasuries held their ground.

WTI rose 2.20% to $70.75 and Brent gained 1.61% to $73.15 as markets approached renewed US-Iran talks after both sides halted attacks and vessels continued through Hormuz. Their monthly declines were still 19.01% and 20.53%. The daily bounce accompanied higher breakevens without undoing the preceding energy-price relief.

DXY fell 0.25% to 101.11 and gold declined 1.38% to $4,022.30. Falling volatility and gold, rising stocks and positive corporate and EM bond returns pointed to less immediate demand for protection. The Treasury curve's modest flattening occurred within that recovery in risk appetite.

## Jobs, European Inflation and the Quarter-End Funding Test

JOLTS and Conference Board confidence are due June 30 at 10:00 ET, followed by the Dallas Fed retail survey at 10:30. ADP, the New York Fed labor-tightness measure, construction spending and ISM manufacturing arrive July 1. Payrolls and initial claims follow July 2 at 8:30. Hiring, vacancies and selling prices will help determine whether Dallas's strong employment reading extends beyond one region.

German unemployment and flash CPI arrive June 30, then euro-area flash HICP July 1, while the Sintra forum continues. US-Iran talks are set to resume in Doha, with shipping through Hormuz still central to the energy outlook. The July 1 BOJ Tankan adds business investment and price expectations to Japan's currency and policy debate.

Treasury sells $80 billion of six-week bills June 30, followed by the regular 17-week sale July 1 and four- and eight-week auctions July 2 at 11:30 ET. Monday's 91- and 182-day issues settle July 2, when payrolls precede the auctions and fixed-income trading is scheduled to close at 14:00. Bill yields, dealer retention and secured funding will show whether money-market inflows can continue to offset the competing demand for equity financing through that concentrated cash transfer.

Dallas manufacturers reported slower output and orders but stronger hiring and selling prices.

US jobs data, European inflation and quarter-end funding now share a calendar shortened by the July 2 early close.
